unitOverview.bigIdea: Les histoires d'automne nous connectent à la nature et aux traditions
unitOverview.culminatingTask: Livre d'histoires d'automne de la classe

lessons.title: L'automne arrive!
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize autumn vocabulary through seasonal objects, visual supports, and nature exploration

activities: Welcome circle with autumn greeting song
Show mystery nature basket - let students guess what's inside
Introduce key word 'automne' with gestures (arms spread wide like season embracing us)
opening.flexibility: If students are very curious about basket contents, extend discovery time and shorten main activity

activities: Nature walk around school grounds (15 min) - collect leaves, observe changes
Return to classroom for leaf exploration (12 min) - touch, sort by color, describe with simple French
Create class 'Autumn Arrived' display with collected items

storyCircle.setup: Students sit in circle with nature treasures in center
storyCircle.props: Real leaves, small pumpkin, autumn-colored scarves
storyCircle.narrative: Simple story about autumn's arrival using collected objects as characters

mainActivity.artIntegration: Students create leaf rubbings while practicing color vocabulary
decisionPoints: If weather prevents outdoor walk: Use window observations and pre-collected materials
If students find many interesting objects: Allow extra sharing time
If attention wanes: Add movement breaks between activities

activities: Share one autumn discovery from our walk
Learn simple autumn gesture routine
Preview tomorrow's leaf dancing adventure

differentiation.languageSupport: Gestures for all vocabulary, visual cards, hands-on manipulation
differentiation.extension: Students lead nature walk observations, create leaf categories

assessment.observational: Note student engagement with vocabulary, comfort with outdoor exploration
assessment.formative: Simple thumbs up/down for vocabulary recognition

lessons.realWorldConnection: How people notice and talk about changing seasons in their daily lives
lessons.culturalElements: Discuss how autumn looks in different French-speaking regions

lessons.title: Les feuilles dansent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand leaf-related vocabulary through movement, colors, and creative expression

activities: Review yesterday's autumn vocabulary with gestures
Introduce today's color words with real leaves
Demonstrate 'tomber' with gentle leaf dropping motion
Leaf dancing activity (10 min) - students move like falling leaves to music
Story circle with leaf puppet show (10 min)
Collaborative leaf art creation (7 min)

storyCircle.setup: Circle with colorful leaf props in center
storyCircle.props: Large felt leaves, small basket, wind sound maker
storyCircle.narrative: Story of leaves dancing in wind, each color having personality
storyCircle.interaction: Students help leaves 'dance' and make wind sounds

mainActivity.artIntegration: Create leaf collage while naming colors in French
mainActivity.dramaticPlay: Students become different colored leaves, act out falling and dancing
decisionPoints: If students love dancing: Extend movement time, reduce art time
If students need calm: Start with gentle movements, build energy gradually
If weather permits: Take leaf dancing outside

activities: Gentle leaf meditation - students close eyes and imagine being autumn leaf
Share favorite leaf color from today
Preview tomorrow's tree exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Color-coded visual supports, movement reinforces vocabulary
differentiation.extension: Students create leaf dance choreography, teach moves to others

assessment.observational: Note color vocabulary recognition during movement
assessment.formative: Students point to correct colored leaves when named

lessons.realWorldConnection: Observing how leaves change and fall in our neighborhood and parks
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by deepening leaf vocabulary while adding movement and color concepts

lessons.title: Les arbres en automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize tree vocabulary through observation, drawing, and simple descriptions

activities: Look out window at real trees while saying 'arbre'
Use arms to show 'branches' extending from body trunk
Practice 'grand' by reaching up high like tall tree
Tree observation walk or window study (8 min)
Story circle about tree's autumn transformation (10 min)
Create tree art with cotton swab painting (9 min)

storyCircle.setup: Sit under or near visible tree, or create tree corner with branch props
storyCircle.props: Tree puppet, felt leaves to add/remove, seasonal clothing for tree
storyCircle.narrative: Story of tree changing clothes from green to autumn colors
storyCircle.interaction: Students help dress/undress tree for seasons

mainActivity.artIntegration: Students paint autumn trees using cotton swabs for leaves
mainActivity.natureWalk: Focus on tree shapes, sizes, and seasonal changes visible around school
decisionPoints: If students fascinated by tree details: Allow more observation time
If restless during story: Add more physical tree movements
If painting gets messy: Simplify to finger printing or stickers

activities: Share tree drawings and use new vocabulary to describe
Practice tree growing movement from seed to full size
Preview tomorrow's weather exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual tree parts diagram, gestures for size concepts
differentiation.extension: Students create tree fact book, measure and compare tree sizes

assessment.observational: Listen for tree vocabulary during art sharing
assessment.formative: Students point to tree parts when vocabulary is said

lessons.realWorldConnection: How trees provide homes for animals and beauty in our communities
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by expanding from individual leaves to whole trees while reinforcing colors and movement

lessons.title: Il fait frais!
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand autumn weather vocabulary through clothing, sensory experiences, and weather observation

activities: Feel the air outside door or window
Demonstrate 'frais' with gentle shiver and cozy wrap gesture
Look for 'nuages' in today's sky
Weather station exploration (8 min) - observe and record today's weather
Story circle about autumn weather changes (10 min)
Dress-up activity for autumn weather (9 min)

storyCircle.setup: Circle with weather prop collection in center
storyCircle.props: Wind maker (fan), cloud cotton, jacket, umbrella, sun prop
storyCircle.narrative: Story of weather changing from summer to autumn
storyCircle.interaction: Students experience each weather type with props and movements

mainActivity.artIntegration: Create weather collage with cotton ball clouds and tissue paper wind
mainActivity.sensoryExperience: Feel different temperatures, air movement, and textures
decisionPoints: If very windy day: Spend more time outside experiencing real wind
If students cold: Bring activity inside and use props for wind
If clothing activity overwhelming: Use just one item per student

activities: Share what clothes we need for today's weather
Practice weather vocabulary with matching movements
Preview tomorrow's animal preparation exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Real weather experience reinforces abstract vocabulary
differentiation.extension: Students become classroom weather reporters, predict tomorrow's weather

assessment.observational: Note weather vocabulary use during dress-up activity
assessment.formative: Students choose appropriate clothing for described weather

lessons.realWorldConnection: How autumn weather affects our clothing choices and daily activities
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by connecting trees and leaves to weather changes while introducing sensory vocabulary

lessons.title: Les animaux se préparent
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn about autumn animal behaviors through stories, movements, and visual supports

activities: Introduce animal friends with puppets
Demonstrate 'préparer' by packing pretend suitcase
Practice animal movements for écureuil and oiseau
Animal preparation story circle (12 min)
Animal movement and preparation game (10 min)
Create animal winter preparation art (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Forest scene with animal homes (boxes/baskets)
storyCircle.props: Squirrel puppet, bird puppet, acorns, nest materials
storyCircle.narrative: Story of animals getting ready for winter - squirrel gathering, bird migrating
storyCircle.interaction: Students help animals prepare by gathering food and building nests

mainActivity.dramaticPlay: Students become animals preparing for winter through movements and actions
mainActivity.natureConnection: Discuss what real animals do in our area during autumn
decisionPoints: If students love animal movements: Extend movement time, add more animals
If story too long: Break into shorter segments with more interaction
If outdoor animals visible: Take brief observation break

activities: Share which animal preparation strategy we think is smartest
Practice all animal movements with vocabulary
Preview tomorrow's first autumn story time

differentiation.languageSupport: Animal movements reinforce vocabulary, visual animal cards
differentiation.extension: Students research local animals, create animal preparation guide

assessment.observational: Watch for animal vocabulary during movement activities
assessment.formative: Students demonstrate animal preparations when prompted

lessons.realWorldConnection: Observing how animals in our area get ready for colder weather
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by introducing animals while connecting to weather and seasonal changes

lessons.title: Première histoire d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will listen to and respond to their first simple autumn story through pictures and gestures

activities: Create cozy story circle with cushions
Introduce story time routine with special story stick
Practice 'écouter' and 'regarder' with exaggerated gestures
Read autumn story with interactive props (15 min)
Story response activity with pictures (8 min)
Begin planning our class story (4 min)

storyCircle.setup: Intimate circle with dim lighting and autumn decorations
storyCircle.props: Story book, character puppets, seasonal objects that appear in story
storyCircle.narrative: Simple autumn adventure story with repetitive phrases and clear pictures
storyCircle.interaction: Students help tell story by providing sound effects and movements

mainActivity.artIntegration: Students draw favorite story moment while retelling in French
mainActivity.oralLanguageDevelopment: Encourage story predictions and simple retellings
decisionPoints: If students very engaged: Read story twice with different focus
If attention wandering: Pause for movement breaks between story sections
If students want to share: Allow brief personal connections to story

activities: Share favorite part of story using pictures or gestures
Practice story vocabulary with movements
Preview meeting story characters tomorrow

differentiation.languageSupport: Rich visual support, repetitive story structure, interactive elements
differentiation.extension: Students create alternative story endings, act out favorite scenes

assessment.observational: Note story comprehension through responses and participation
assessment.formative: Students point to story elements when mentioned

lessons.realWorldConnection: How families and communities share stories about seasons and nature
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by introducing storytelling while incorporating all previous autumn vocabulary

lessons.title: Les personnages d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify story characters through dramatic play, props, and visual character cards

activities: Greet yesterday's story characters with puppets
Practice describing characters with 'petit' and 'gentil' gestures
Introduce character exploration activity
Character puppet show and discussion (10 min)
Character role-play stations (12 min)
Character trait art activity (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Character gallery with puppets and props displayed
storyCircle.props: Character puppets, trait cards, emotion faces, costume pieces
storyCircle.narrative: Introduce each character's personality through puppet interactions
storyCircle.interaction: Students help characters show different emotions and traits

mainActivity.dramaticPlay: Students try on character roles with simple props and movements
mainActivity.artIntegration: Draw character portraits showing their special traits
decisionPoints: If students love role-playing: Extend dramatic play time
If shy about performing: Use partner work or smaller groups
If characters confusing: Focus on one main character today

activities: Share which character we'd like to be friends with and why
Practice character movements and voices
Preview tomorrow's story events exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual character cards, emotion faces, gesture support
differentiation.extension: Students create new characters, write character descriptions

assessment.observational: Listen for character vocabulary during role-play
assessment.formative: Students identify character traits when shown pictures

lessons.realWorldConnection: How stories help us understand different personalities and feelings
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by deepening story comprehension while introducing character vocabulary and dramatic play

lessons.title: Que se passe-t-il?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand story events through sequencing, retelling, and simple cause-and-effect activities

activities: Review story from previous lessons using pictures
Introduce sequence words with hand gestures (first, then, now)
Practice timeline concept with daily routine examples
Story sequence activity with timeline (10 min)
Retelling story circle with props (12 min)
Cause and effect exploration (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Story timeline displayed around circle with prop stations
storyCircle.props: Sequence cards, story timeline, event props, retelling cube
storyCircle.narrative: Collaborative retelling using sequence vocabulary and student participation
storyCircle.interaction: Students place events in order and explain what happens next

mainActivity.oralLanguageDevelopment: Practice using sequence words to tell simple stories
mainActivity.artIntegration: Create story maps showing beginning, middle, and end
decisionPoints: If sequencing challenging: Use only 3 main events today
If students love retelling: Allow multiple versions of same story
If timeline confusing: Act out sequence with body movements

activities: Practice sequence vocabulary with daily routine events
Share what happens 'après' school today
Preview tomorrow's vocabulary practice games

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual sequence supports, gesture cues for time words
differentiation.extension: Students create personal daily sequence stories, predict story outcomes

assessment.observational: Note use of sequence vocabulary during retelling
assessment.formative: Students arrange story events in correct order

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how events connect in our daily lives and experiences
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by adding sequence vocabulary while practicing character identification and story comprehension

lessons.title: Mes mots d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will practice autumn vocabulary through word games, picture matching, and creative expression

activities: Open vocabulary treasure box with previously learned words
Practice 'dire' and 'répéter' with echo games
Introduce word appreciation concept
Vocabulary review stations (15 min) - rotate through word games
Word appreciation circle (8 min)
Create personal word collection (4 min)

storyCircle.setup: Circle surrounded by vocabulary stations with game materials
storyCircle.props: Word treasure box, picture cards, movement props, memory game
storyCircle.narrative: Story about words being treasures we collect and share
storyCircle.interaction: Students share favorite words and demonstrate meanings

mainActivity.gameBasedLearning: Vocabulary bingo, memory matching, movement games
mainActivity.artIntegration: Students illustrate favorite autumn words in personal journals
decisionPoints: If games too exciting: Use calmer activities like matching
If students struggling: Focus on 5-7 key vocabulary words
If wanting more challenge: Add rhyming or word family activities

activities: Share our favorite autumn 'mot' from today's collection
Practice saying words with different emotions (happy, surprised, quiet)
Preview tomorrow's collaborative storytelling adventure

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual word cards, gesture support, repetition through games
differentiation.extension: Students create word families, make rhyming word pairs

assessment.observational: Note vocabulary retention during games and activities
assessment.formative: Students match pictures to vocabulary words independently

lessons.realWorldConnection: How learning new words helps us express our thoughts and feelings
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by consolidating vocabulary while introducing meta-language concepts about words and communication

lessons.title: Raconter ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students will participate in collaborative storytelling through turns, prompts, and shared creative expression

activities: Introduce collaborative storytelling with talking stick
Practice 'tour' concept with simple sharing circle
Demonstrate 'raconter' and 'ensemble' through group gesture
Practice turn-taking with simple story starters (8 min)
Collaborative autumn story creation (15 min)
Story celebration and sharing (4 min)

storyCircle.setup: Circle with story building materials and talking stick in center
storyCircle.props: Story starter cards, autumn vocabulary props, talking stick, poster paper
storyCircle.narrative: Students build story together, each adding one element
storyCircle.interaction: Turn-taking structure with visual and verbal supports

mainActivity.oralLanguageDevelopment: Structured practice in story construction and turn-taking
mainActivity.dramaticPlay: Act out parts of collaborative story as it develops
decisionPoints: If students shy about contributing: Use picture prompts or whisper to teacher
If story getting complex: Simplify with 'and then...' structure
If some students dominating: Use timer or gesture cues for turns

activities: Celebrate our first group story creation
Practice turn-taking vocabulary with class routine examples
Preview tomorrow's autumn sounds exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual turn-taking cues, story prompt pictures, gesture supports
differentiation.extension: Students create story illustrations, retell story to other classes

assessment.observational: Note turn-taking skills and story contribution comfort level
assessment.formative: Students demonstrate understanding of 'tour' in other contexts

lessons.realWorldConnection: How families and friends create stories together during conversations and activities
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by encouraging oral expression while practicing vocabulary and story structure concepts

lessons.title: Les sons d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore autumn sounds through listening activities, sound-making, and vocabulary reinforcement
materials: Autumn sound effect materials (leaves, sticks, paper)

activities: Moment of 'silence' to appreciate quiet sounds around us
Introduce 'entendre' by cupping ears and listening carefully
Practice making different autumn 'bruits' with materials
Autumn sound exploration walk (10 min)
Sound story creation circle (12 min)
Sound identification game (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Circle with sound-making materials and listening props
storyCircle.props: Leaves for rustling, sticks for tapping, wind chimes, rain sounds
storyCircle.narrative: Create story using autumn sounds as characters and plot elements
storyCircle.interaction: Students add sound effects as story develops

mainActivity.natureWalk: Focus on listening for autumn sounds - leaves rustling, wind, birds
mainActivity.artIntegration: Create sound artwork - drawings inspired by different autumn sounds
decisionPoints: If outdoor sounds limited: Create autumn sounds indoors with materials
If students overwhelmed by sounds: Use quieter activities and smaller groups
If very engaged with sound exploration: Extend listening time

activities: Share favorite autumn sound from our exploration
Practice sound vocabulary with whisper and loud voice variations
Preview tomorrow's class story creation beginning

differentiation.languageSupport: Auditory vocabulary reinforced through actual sound experiences
differentiation.extension: Students record autumn sounds, create sound compositions

assessment.observational: Note sound vocabulary use during exploration activities
assessment.formative: Students identify sounds when heard without visual cues

lessons.realWorldConnection: How different seasons bring different sounds to our environment
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by adding auditory elements to storytelling while reinforcing autumn vocabulary and oral expression

lessons.title: Notre histoire de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students will begin creating a class autumn story through collaboration, illustration, and vocabulary application

activities: Review all autumn vocabulary learned so far
Introduce concept of 'notre' story belonging to everyone
Brainstorm what our class autumn story might include
Story planning session (10 min) - choose characters, setting, events
Begin story creation and illustration (15 min)
Share progress and plan next steps (2 min)

storyCircle.setup: Collaborative workspace with story materials spread around circle
storyCircle.props: Large book template, art supplies, vocabulary cards, planning chart
storyCircle.narrative: Begin creating original class story incorporating all learned vocabulary

mainActivity.artIntegration: Students collaborate on illustrations that support story text
mainActivity.oralLanguageDevelopment: Practice using all autumn vocabulary in creative context
decisionPoints: If story planning overwhelming: Use teacher-guided prompts and choices
If artistic abilities vary greatly: Focus on effort and vocabulary use
If students want very different stories: Find common elements to blend

activities: Admire our story beginning and celebrate collaborative work
Practice 'créer' and 'dessiner' vocabulary through gesture
Preview tomorrow's learning review and preparation for sharing

differentiation.languageSupport: Vocabulary cards available for reference, visual story planning
differentiation.extension: Students create individual story pages, add detailed illustrations

assessment.observational: Note vocabulary application during story creation
assessment.formative: Students contribute meaningfully to collaborative story planning

lessons.realWorldConnection: How communities work together to create and share meaningful stories
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by synthesizing all previous learning into creative production while practicing collaborative skills

lessons.title: Révision et célébration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate autumn vocabulary understanding through review activities, games, and assessment opportunities

activities: Celebrate how much we have learned with 'savoir' gestures
Practice 'apprendre' by reviewing lesson highlights
Acknowledge everyone doing 'bien' in their own way
Vocabulary review stations (15 min) - games and activities from unit
Individual assessment conversations (8 min)
Group celebration preparation (4 min)

storyCircle.setup: Celebration circle with all unit materials and achievements displayed
storyCircle.props: Vocabulary cards, artwork from unit, story elements, achievement symbols
storyCircle.narrative: Review learning journey through unit materials and memories
storyCircle.interaction: Students share favorite learning moments and vocabulary

mainActivity.assessment: Gentle individual conversations about vocabulary recognition and story comprehension
mainActivity.artIntegration: Create portfolio page showing autumn learning journey
decisionPoints: If students need more review: Focus on 5-7 core vocabulary words
If assessment anxiety appears: Make conversations very informal and supportive
If celebration energy high: Allow more time for sharing and recognition

activities: Recognize each student's learning growth and effort
Practice reflection vocabulary while looking at our work
Preview tomorrow's exciting story book presentation

differentiation.languageSupport: Portfolio visual supports, choice in demonstration methods
differentiation.extension: Students create teaching materials to share learning with others

assessment.observational: Comprehensive observation of vocabulary use and story comprehension
assessment.formative: Individual conversations about learning progress and favorite activities

lessons.realWorldConnection: How reflecting on our learning helps us grow and feel proud of our progress
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by reviewing and consolidating all core learning while preparing for final demonstration

lessons.title: Présentation du livre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will present their class autumn book through sharing, reading aloud, and celebrating collaborative achievement

activities: Practice 'présenter' with confident posture and clear voice
Prepare to 'partager' our story with others
Acknowledge feeling 'fier' of our collaborative work
Story presentation preparation (5 min)
Class book sharing presentation (15 min)
Audience appreciation and celebration (7 min)

storyCircle.setup: Presentation area with audience seating and book display
storyCircle.props: Completed class book, presentation stand, celebration materials
storyCircle.narrative: Students present their collaborative autumn story to audience
storyCircle.interaction: Shared reading with each student contributing to presentation

mainActivity.oralLanguageDevelopment: Authentic presentation practice with meaningful audience
mainActivity.communityBuilding: Celebrate collaborative achievement and individual contributions
decisionPoints: If students nervous about presenting: Use shared reading approach
If no outside audience available: Present to other class or stuffed animal audience
If students want individual recognition: Acknowledge specific contributions

activities: Celebrate our presentation success and learning journey
Thank audience and share appreciation for support
Preview exciting extension activities coming in following lessons

differentiation.languageSupport: Shared presentation reduces individual pressure, visual book support
differentiation.extension: Students create individual story pages, plan additional performances

assessment.observational: Note confidence and vocabulary use during presentation
assessment.summative: Evaluation of overall autumn vocabulary acquisition and story comprehension

lessons.realWorldConnection: How sharing our creations builds confidence and connects us with others
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by culminating core curriculum through authentic presentation and celebration of learning

lessons.title: Contes traditionnels d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore traditional autumn stories from French culture through listening, discussion, and cultural connection (extension)

activities: Introduce concept of 'traditionnel' stories passed down through families
Show 'culture' through pictures of French-speaking communities
Practice 'autrefois' with gestures showing long ago time
Listen to traditional French autumn story (12 min)
Cultural exploration and comparison (10 min)
Create cultural appreciation art (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Cultural circle with French artifacts and traditional story materials
storyCircle.props: Traditional story book, cultural artifacts, map, comparison pictures
storyCircle.narrative: Traditional autumn story from French-speaking culture
storyCircle.interaction: Compare traditional elements to our own experiences

mainActivity.culturalExploration: Discuss how different cultures celebrate and understand autumn
mainActivity.artIntegration: Create art inspired by traditional story elements
decisionPoints: If traditional story too complex: Focus on visual elements and simple themes
If students making many connections: Allow more comparison discussion time
If cultural concepts abstract: Use concrete examples and pictures

activities: Share what we found interesting about traditional story
Practice cultural vocabulary with appreciation gestures
Preview tomorrow's drama and performance activities

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual cultural supports, comparison to familiar experiences
differentiation.extension: Students research family traditions, create cultural story collection

assessment.observational: Note cultural vocabulary understanding and story engagement
assessment.formative: Students identify traditional elements in stories

lessons.realWorldConnection: How different cultures have special stories about autumn and harvest time
lessons.progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - deepens cultural understanding while practicing story comprehension skills

lessons.title: Théâtre d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will perform simple autumn scenes through dramatic play, costumes, and creative expression (extension)

activities: Transform classroom into theater space
Practice 'jouer' through simple character movements
Introduce 'spectacle' and 'rôle' concepts through demonstration
Choose roles and prepare costumes (8 min)
Rehearse autumn scenes (12 min)
Perform mini-theater presentations (7 min)

storyCircle.setup: Theater circle with performance area and costume station
storyCircle.props: Costumes, autumn scene backdrops, character props, simple scripts
storyCircle.narrative: Students create and perform short autumn scenes
storyCircle.interaction: Audience participation and appreciation of performances

mainActivity.dramaticPlay: Structured dramatic expression using autumn vocabulary and themes
mainActivity.performanceArts: Introduction to theater concepts through age-appropriate activities
decisionPoints: If students nervous about performing: Use group scenes and familiar characters
If very enthusiastic about drama: Allow more rehearsal and creative time
If costumes overwhelming: Use simple props or just movements

activities: Appreciate all performances and creative choices
Practice theater vocabulary through performance reflection
Preview tomorrow's poetry and rhythm exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Movement and costume support vocabulary expression
differentiation.extension: Students write simple scripts, create elaborate costume designs

assessment.observational: Note creative expression and theater vocabulary use
assessment.formative: Students demonstrate understanding of performance concepts

lessons.realWorldConnection: How acting and drama help us understand different perspectives and express creativity
lessons.progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - applies story knowledge through kinesthetic and dramatic expression

lessons.title: Poésie d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore autumn poetry through rhythm, rhyme, and creative language play (extension)

activities: Experience 'rythme' through clapping and movement
Discover 'rime' through simple word pairs that sound alike
Introduce 'poème' as special way to play with words
Listen to autumn poetry with rhythm (10 min)
Create simple class poem together (12 min)
Illustrate and share poetry (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Poetry circle with rhythm instruments and word play materials
storyCircle.props: Poetry books, rhythm instruments, rhyming cards, illustration materials
storyCircle.narrative: Explore different autumn poems with rhythm and movement
storyCircle.interaction: Students add rhythm and movement to poetry experience

mainActivity.musicIntegration: Use rhythm and rhyme to enhance language learning
mainActivity.artIntegration: Create visual poetry through illustration and creative expression
decisionPoints: If rhythm activities too exciting: Use gentler clapping and movement
If rhyming difficult: Focus on rhythm and word appreciation
If students love poetry creation: Allow more time for individual poems

activities: Share our class poem creation with rhythm performance
Practice poetry vocabulary through gentle movement
Preview tomorrow's legends and mystery story exploration

differentiation.languageSupport: Rhythm reinforces language patterns, visual poetry support
differentiation.extension: Students create individual poems, perform poetry for other classes

assessment.observational: Note poetry vocabulary understanding and rhythm participation
assessment.formative: Students identify rhyme and rhythm in simple poems

lessons.realWorldConnection: How poetry helps us express feelings about nature and seasonal changes
lessons.progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - introduces poetic language while reinforcing autumn vocabulary and oral expression

lessons.title: Légendes d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will discover autumn legends and myths through storytelling, imagination, and cultural exploration (extension)

activities: Create mysterious atmosphere for 'légende' introduction
Practice 'magique' through wonder and amazement gestures
Introduce 'mystère' concept through guessing games
Listen to autumn legend with magical elements (12 min)
Explore mystery and magic in nature (10 min)
Begin creating class legend (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: Mystical circle with dim lighting and magical props
storyCircle.props: Legend books, magical storytelling objects, mystery boxes, cultural artifacts
storyCircle.narrative: Traditional autumn legend with magical and mysterious elements
storyCircle.interaction: Students participate in magical story elements and wonder discussions

mainActivity.imaginativePlay: Explore concepts of magic and mystery through safe, age-appropriate activities
mainActivity.culturalExploration: Discuss how legends help communities understand nature
decisionPoints: If legends too mysterious for some: Focus on nature wonder rather than supernatural
If students very engaged with magic: Allow more imaginative exploration time
If concepts too abstract: Use concrete examples and familiar comparisons

activities: Share what made the legend special and interesting
Practice legend vocabulary through storytelling gestures
Preview tomorrow's exploration of autumn around the world

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual mystery supports, wonder-based vocabulary introduction
differentiation.extension: Students create family legends, explore cultural mythology

assessment.observational: Note legend vocabulary understanding and imaginative engagement
assessment.formative: Students distinguish between real and legendary story elements

lessons.realWorldConnection: How legends help communities explain natural phenomena and preserve cultural wisdom
lessons.progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - expands story genres while practicing vocabulary and comprehension skills

lessons.title: Automne autour du monde
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore how autumn is celebrated in different French-speaking regions through photos, stories, and cultural comparison (extension)

activities: Explore our big 'monde' using world map and pictures
Identify different 'pays' where French is spoken
Practice 'différent' by comparing local autumn to other places
Virtual journey to French-speaking autumn regions (12 min)
Compare autumn celebrations and traditions (10 min)
Create world autumn appreciation art (5 min)

storyCircle.setup: World exploration circle with map, photos, and cultural materials
storyCircle.props: World map, autumn photos from different regions, cultural artifacts, music
storyCircle.narrative: Journey through different French-speaking regions experiencing autumn
storyCircle.interaction: Students compare autumn experiences and ask questions about different places

mainActivity.globalAwareness: Develop appreciation for diverse autumn experiences worldwide
mainActivity.artIntegration: Create artwork showing autumn diversity around the world
decisionPoints: If global concepts overwhelming: Focus on 2-3 specific regions
If students very curious about places: Allow more exploration and question time
If comparison difficult: Use simple same/different activities

activities: Share most interesting autumn discovery from our world journey
Practice global vocabulary through appreciation gestures
Preview tomorrow's final celebration and festival planning

differentiation.languageSupport: Visual global supports, comparison to familiar experiences
differentiation.extension: Students research specific countries, create travel brochures

assessment.observational: Note global vocabulary understanding and cultural curiosity
assessment.formative: Students identify similarities and differences in autumn celebrations

lessons.realWorldConnection: How people around the world experience and celebrate autumn in diverse ways
lessons.progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - broadens cultural perspective while applying autumn vocabulary in global contexts

lessons.title: Notre festival d'automne
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their autumn learning journey through a festival combining stories, activities, and community sharing (extension)

activities: Transform classroom into 'festival' celebration space
Practice 'célébrer' through joyful movements and expressions
Welcome our learning 'communauté' to the festival
Festival station activities (15 min) - showcase all unit learning
Community appreciation ceremony (8 min)
Festival reflection and memory creation (4 min)

storyCircle.setup: Festival center with all unit creations and learning displayed
storyCircle.props: All unit artifacts, student work, celebration materials, memory book
storyCircle.narrative: Celebration of complete learning journey through autumn stories
